summary: Madimba territory (Kongo-Central) lies south-west of Kinshasa along the Kinshasa-Matadi RN1 road and railway, with Kisantu as its main town and the rural Ngidinga and Nselo secteurs to the south and east. It is far from the eastern conflict zones and no armed group holds territory. Towns and villages are under ordinary state control, with the PNC as the main force and customary chiefs settling local disputes; FARDC elements pass along the corridor. Security issues are crime and sporadic political-religious (Bundu dia Kongo) unrest that do not amount to territorial control. Web search was unavailable for this run, so the assessment rests on default state presence.

zones.description: Kisantu town (cité, Kisantu health zone) and its neighbourhoods Nkandu, Nzeza Nlandu, Kikonka, Gare
zones.evidence: Kisantu is the main town of Madimba territory on the Kinshasa-Matadi RN1 road and railway, ~120 km from Kinshasa, far from the eastern conflict zones; no armed group is known to hold territory. Order is kept by the PNC under the state administration; petty urban crime and occasional Bundu dia Kongo-related unrest in Kongo-Central do not amount to territorial control. Web search was unavailable for this run (session search budget exhausted), so this rests on default state presence.

zones.description: Other towns and villages of Kisantu secteur and the northern Nselo health zone (Mangongolo, Ntadintadi, Mbuba, Madimba, Nselo, Kinkangu, Ngufu, Tombo, Kilenda etc.)
zones.evidence: Settlements along or near the RN1/railway corridor and the Inkisi valley in a calm western province with no reported armed-group activity; PNC posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs handle order and disputes. Web search was unavailable for this run (session search budget exhausted), so this rests on default state presence.

zones.description: Rural southern Madimba: Ngidinga and Nselo secteurs (Ngidinga cité/Suika, Kilua cité, Kiniangi, Kinkosi, Kindundu and surrounding villages)
zones.evidence: Remote rural secteurs south and east of Kisantu; no source located on any armed group holding territory. State presence is thin (PNC posts in secteur centres, customary chiefs in villages), so assigned to the PNC by default with low confidence. Web search was unavailable for this run (session search budget exhausted), so this rests on default state presence.
